testCase.description: DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: example "intersection([1,2],[2,3], [2,3,4]) = [2]". Normative example of the new intersection function (DMN17-98). Single-element result, so order does not matter.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: example "intersection(["a","b","c"],["a","b"]) = ["a", "b"]". The result order is unspecified ("in no particular order"), so the expectation is order-independent: the result is sorted with sort(list, precedes) (§10.3.4.9) before comparison.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: example "intersection(["a","b","c"],["a","b"]) = ["a", "b"]". The result order is unspecified ("in no particular order"), so the expectation is order-independent: this case checks the size only.
DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: example "intersection([1],[2]) = []". Normative example: disjoint lists give the empty list.
DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: example "intersection([1,2,3], null) = null". Normative example: a null argument gives null.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4: "Whenever a parameter is outside its domain, the result of the built-in is null." DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: parameter domain "list"; mirrors the normative example intersection([1,2,3], null) = null. Derived: null as the first argument also gives null.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: intersection(list...): "return the common elements of the lists in no particular order with duplicate removal". Derived: duplicates present in every list appear once in the result. Single-element result, so order does not matter.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: intersection(list...): "return the common elements of the lists in no particular order with duplicate removal". Derived: intersecting with an empty list gives the empty list.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: intersection(list...): "return the common elements of the lists in no particular order with duplicate removal". Derived: several common elements. The result order is unspecified ("in no particular order"), so the expectation is order-independent: the result is sorted before comparison.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: intersection(list...): "return the common elements of the lists in no particular order with duplicate removal". §10.3.2.15 Table 54: string equality: "e1 is the same sequence of characters as e2". Derived: string elements are compared with FEEL string equality, which is case sensitive, so "a" and "A" are not common.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: intersection(list...): "return the common elements of the lists in no particular order with duplicate removal". §10.3.2.15 Table 53: e1 = e2 requires "e1 and e2 must both be of the same kind/datatype". Derived: elements of different types are never equal (1 and "1" are not the same element), so only the string "1" is common. Single-element result.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: intersection(list...): "return the common elements of the lists in no particular order with duplicate removal". §10.3.2.15 Table 54: number equality: "value(e1) = value(e2) ... Precision is not considered." Derived: numbers are compared by FEEL numeric equality (1.0 = 1), so 1.0 and 1 are a common element. Single-element result.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: intersection(list...): "return the common elements of the lists in no particular order with duplicate removal". §10.3.2.15 Table 54: list equality: "lists must be same length N and e1[i] = e2[i] for 1 ≤ i ≤ N." Derived: list elements are compared with FEEL list equality, so the nested list [1,2] is common and is kept as one element (not flattened). Single-element result.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: intersection(list...): "return the common elements of the lists in no particular order with duplicate removal"; "list..." accepts a variable number of lists. Derived: with a single list every element is common, so the result is that list with duplicate removal. The result order is unspecified ("in no particular order"), so the expectation is order-independent: the result is sorted before comparison.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: intersection(list...): "return the common elements of the lists in no particular order with duplicate removal"; §10.3.2.15 Table 54: context equality: "contexts must have same set of keys K and e1.k = e2.k for every k in K". Derived: only {a: 1} is common. Single-element result, so order does not matter.

DMN 1.7 beta 1 §10.3.4.4 Table 76: intersection(list...): "return the common elements of the lists". Derived: an element must be in every list; 2 and 3 are each shared by only two of the three lists, so the result is empty.
